script.title: The Man Who Signed Machu Picchu Nine Years Before Bingham
sentences: A man signed Machu Picchu in charcoal in 1902.
The Inca built it around 1450, and the jungle later grew over it.
Peruvian explorer Agustín Lizárraga cleared undergrowth for hours to reach the stone buildings.
He wrote "A. Lizárraga 1902" on the Temple of the Three Windows.
In 1911, a villager led American Hiram Bingham to the same ruins.
Bingham saw the name and wrote in his pocket journal that Lizárraga was the discoverer.
Later he played that down, and in his 1952 book he claimed he found it himself.
His own journal had already named the discoverer.
script.description:
Machu Picchu had a name in charcoal on its wall before Hiram Bingham arrived.
His own journal said who got there first.
visuals: Machu Picchu Temple of the Three Windows
claims_en: Agustín Lizárraga marked his surname and the year 1902 in charcoal at Machu Picchu
Machu Picchu was built around 1450 by the Inca
Over the centuries the surrounding jungle overgrew the site
Lizárraga was a Peruvian explorer whose 1902 expedition cleared undergrowth for several hours to reach the stone structures
He wrote 'A. Lizárraga 1902' on the central window of the Temple of the Three Windows
In 1911 a villager led Hiram Bingham to Machu Picchu
Bingham found Lizárraga's surname and the 1902 date
Bingham wrote in his pocket field journal that Agustín Lizárraga is discoverer of Machu Picchu
Bingham gradually downplayed Lizárraga's role, and in Lost City of the Incas (1952) claimed to have found the site himself
